title: The boss and the worker
hook: authority is service, and work is owed honestly
tomorrow: what do you say to someone who just lost their job?

segments.voice: Yesterday, colleagues: four friends on a roof, one corner each. The line was neighbors at work.

The schedule drops late again. The manager wants just ten more minutes after you've clocked out. Or flip it around: the coworker who disappears on breaks while the line grows and someone else covers. Every job is a deal with two sides, and either side can cheat. Jesus speaks to the side with the power first.
screen: `TEN MORE MINUTES, OFF THE CLOCK.` → `THE ONE WHO DISAPPEARS.` → `TWO SIDES OF ONE DEAL.`

segments.voice: His disciples are arguing about who will be greatest. He tells them that among the nations, rulers lord it over people, but it isn't to be that way with them: "whosoever will be first among you, shall be the servant of all." Authority, in that picture, is a job of serving the people under you. And the other side? When Jesus sends out disciples, he tells them to take what they're given, "for the labourer is worthy of his hire." Pay is owed, not a favor. Catholic social teaching holds both ends. Pope Leo the Thirteenth wrote that a worker should carry out fully and faithfully the work freely agreed to, and that an employer must never treat workers as mere tools and must give each a just wage. The Catechism names wrongs on both sides in plain words: paying unjust wages breaks the commandment against stealing, and so does work poorly done. Not a war between bosses and workers, and not blind obedience either. Each owes the other something real. Here's the thing to tell a friend: in the Catechism, work poorly done and unjust wages sit in the same paragraph.
screen: `THE FIRST, THE SERVANT OF ALL.` · `WORTHY OF HIS HIRE.` · `LEO XIII: DUTIES BOTH WAYS.` · `TWO WRONGS, ONE PARAGRAPH.` · then, large: `HONEST ON BOTH SIDES.`

segments.voice: Think of one person above you and one person beside or below you, at work, school or home. Choose one honest thing you owe each of them: a full effort, a fair word, a thank-you. If it fits, send one of them a short message now.
The boss and the worker. Two sides of every job, each owing the other something real.
screen: `THE BOSS AND THE WORKER — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: honest on both sides, service from the top and full effort from the floor. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholic social teaching, from Pope Leo XIII's Rerum Novarum onward, speaks of just wages and honest work; some Catholics bring their work life to confession, examining both how they lead and how they work.

fork.setup: you lead the weekend crew. one worker is great but always ten minutes late. by Mark and the Catechism, what's your move?
options: talk with her honestly and ask what's behind it, as someone who serves the crew.
dock her pay quietly; a boss doesn't owe explanations.
let it go; a good boss never corrects anyone.
fork.reveal: authority is service, and work is owed honestly. a serving boss still names the problem, and asks first.

what it means: honest on both sides: authority as service, and work given fully for a just wage.
what a scholar hears: Mark 10:42–44 against lording it over; Rerum Novarum 20 on mutual duties; CCC 2409 and 2434 on wages and work poorly done.

recall: the job done well, as love

chat.says: Don Luis wants me to clock out, then finish mopping. says everyone did it. i need this job.
options: Mop well while you're on the clock, and ask him kindly to pay for all of it. Honest both ways.
Just do it. Good workers don't make trouble, and the Church says to obey the boss.
Mop badly to even it out. If he won't pay for it, he doesn't get your best.
chat.meaning: The laborer is worthy of his hire, and the Catechism names unjust wages and work poorly done side by side. Each side owes the other.

Leo the Thirteenth.meaning: a pope who wrote on the rights and duties of workers

social teaching.meaning: the Church's teaching on justice in work and society

Catechism.meaning: the Catholic Church's official summary of its teaching

notes: Douay-Rheims Mark 10:44 and Luke 10:7 quoted from memory; confirm exact Challoner wording ('labourer' is the translation's spelling).
Rerum Novarum 20 paraphrased: workers fully and faithfully to perform the work freely and equitably agreed; employers not to treat workers as bondsmen and to give each what is just. Confirm.
CCC 2409 lists 'paying unjust wages' and 'work poorly done' among offenses against the seventh commandment; CCC 2434 on the just wage. Confirm both are in 2409 as the teach says.

Life day: Sofia's boss asks for unpaid work after clock-out. The right reply is honest effort plus a respectful request to be paid; no legal advice is given. A Keeper or the owner may want a gentle 'talk to a parent' line; flagging.
